clue.text: Find one's attention taken by old saw

definitions.meaning: to have your attention gripped is to ..., which split in two gives the answer
an archaic way of saying 'saw', the past tense of behold

explanation.walkthrough: 'old saw' looks like a proverb, but it is the verb 'saw' in old-fashioned dress. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is a literary verb for look at, so its past tense is an antique form of the verb meaning observed.

clue.text: Slight attraction to Beast finally evident in Beauty

indicators.note: these letters show up inside the beauty's word

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
it is sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of Beast

explanation.surface: Beauty is a little drawn to the Beast in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident in' is the container signal. 'Slight' looks like an adjective but is the verb, and Beauty and the Beast form a fairy-tale picture that hides the mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to disparage them or play down their worth.

clue.text: Poor chap needs somewhere to relax with a good book

parts.note: a haven is a place of safety and rest
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A hard-up man wants a quiet spot to curl up and read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Good Book' is the Bible, so OT (Old Testament) is one of it. 'needs' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking wealth, contrasted with the haves.

clue.text: Drops we see in spring garden?

definitions.meaning: foliage open on the trees in springtime

explanation.definitionFit: Omits, and also foliage on view on plants in springtime.

clue.text: Brings up delicacies after due preparation

indicators.note: the delicacies are placed after the prepared letters
preparing the word due means working it into a new order of its letters

parts.note: cates is an old word for dainties or choice foods

explanation.surface: Fine foods are served once everything owed has been made ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparation' signals the anagram of 'due', and 'after' sets the delicacies behind it. Cates is an archaic word for dainty foods, seldom met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise and teach a child is to bring them up, which is schooling in the broad sense.

clue.text: Blow me down!

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise, read literally as a seed head inviting a child to blow its fluffy seeds away

explanation.walkthrough: Children blow the seed head of a weed to 'tell the time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The round fluffy seed head of a common yellow weed.

clue.text: Triumphantly carry off academic position

definitions.meaning: to hoist a winner shoulder-high in celebration

explanation.definitionFit: To lift a victor shoulder-high, and a university professorship.

clue.text: Asian can be brought in by Army

indicators.note: brought in puts the following pieces inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a can
taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: An Asian person might be recruited by the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' is the container signal; the Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Himalayan region north of Nepal.

clue.text: Take apples, say — the poor ones left

definitions.meaning: to steal fruit from an orchard
a dialect word for small withered apples

explanation.walkthrough: Scrumping is British slang for stealing apples from orchards.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for raiding an orchard, and an old word for shrivelled fruit.

clue.text: Anything broken? Send for the Bill. I'd say

definitions.text: Send for the Bill. I'd say
definitions.meaning: a jokey request for the bill; 'the Bill' also suggests British slang for police

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bill' is British slang for the police, the misleading surface after a break-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal question about harm, and a colloquial request for the price.

clue.text: Priest executed prophet, a monster

parts.note: Levi was the ancestor of Israel's priestly tribe, so Levi stands for a priest

indicators.note: executed in the sense of beheaded, so the first letter is cut off the word

parts.note: Nathan was the Old Testament prophet who rebuked King David

explanation.surface: A clergyman put a prophet to death, which was monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' means beheaded: NATHAN loses its first letter to give ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sea beast of Job, now any huge creature or thing.

clue.text: Girl forever in a book — let that be a warning

definitions.meaning: Forever ... is Kathleen Winsor's 1944 novel named after its heroine
the yellow traffic light that warns drivers the red is coming

explanation.walkthrough: Forever Amber is a famous historical romance; the second sense is the British traffic-light colour between green and red.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine's name in a bestselling novel title, and the caution colour of a traffic signal.

clue.text: Backer lost money in something that made a bomb — a touching line

indicators.note: the shortened backer is placed inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive used in bombs

indicators.note: lost means the money letter goes missing from the backer's word

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A financier lost cash in a show that bombed, which touched a nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' signals the deletion and 'in' the container. 'made a bomb' sounds like making a fortune, but here it describes an explosive; a theatrical backer is called an angel.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a straight line that meets a curve at one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Slip resulting in a slip?

parts.note: a printing mistake that leads to a little slip of paper being inserted in a book to correct it

explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word for an error in print, listed on an inserted correction sheet.

clue.text: Almost nimble with old printing method

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: lithe means supple and agile

explanation.surface: An agile person working with an outdated way of printing.
explanation.walkthrough: LITHE without its last letter gives LITH, then O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for lithography, printing from a flat inked stone or plate.

clue.text: Cutting a fringe

definitions.meaning: clipping or pruning, as with hedges or hair
decorative edging sewn on clothes or furnishings

explanation.definitionFit: Both the act of clipping and the ornamental braid or edging on a garment.

clue.text: Illusion of marks on Mars — Schiaparelli's first in the trap

parts.note: mares, used here as an English plural of mare, are the dark plains seen on Mars or the Moon

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Schiaparelli's

explanation.surface: The astronomer Schiaparelli saw markings on Mars that were imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: Schiaparelli mapped Martian markings later shown to be illusory. S goes inside NET. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposed discovery that turns out to be a hoax or delusion.

clue.text: For beauty. Greek island overcomes resident foreigner

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over the other

parts.note: Cos is an island of the Dodecanese
a metic was an alien resident in an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: Something for appearance's sake, as an island defeats an immigrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to improve appearance only.

clue.text: Circular building where there are places for all in the gods

definitions.text: Circular building where there are places for all in the gods

parts.words: Circular building where there are places for all in the gods
parts.note: suggests a round theatre with seats up in the gallery, but means the domed Roman temple to every deity

explanation.walkthrough: 'the gods' is British slang for the cheapest top gallery of a theatre; here it means the deities, all of whom the Roman temple honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: The round domed temple in Rome dedicated to every deity, from Greek for all gods.

clue.text: Get current set of papers

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Buy the latest batch of newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or come to possess.

clue.text: College head almost finds the right page

indicators.note: almost means the title drops its final letter

parts.note: a rector heads some colleges and Scottish universities

explanation.surface: A principal very nearly locates the correct page.
explanation.walkthrough: RECTOR loses its last R. 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book, opposite the verso.

clue.text: It's stimulating to face my superior

indicators.note: superior means placed higher, so in this down entry one piece sits on top

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like 'my!'
a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Standing up to one's boss is exhilarating.
explanation.walkthrough: COR goes above DIAL. 'to' is a link. 'my' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial was a reviving or invigorating drink.

clue.text: Lack of progress with no change under way

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece below goes after the one above

parts.note: ST is an abbreviation for street
as is means unaltered

explanation.surface: Things stand still as a project begins unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: ASIS goes under ST. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation or equilibrium.

clue.text: It's drunk quite a lot initially

definitions.text: It's drunk quite a lot initially

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of lot

explanation.surface: A spirit that people knock back in quantity at the start of a night.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITE plus A plus L (the first letter of 'lot') is rearranged under 'drunk'; the whole clue also describes the Mexican spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican spirit distilled from agave, typically taken in shots.

clue.text: Some attack bowling, others block

indicators.note: some means a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some batsmen hit out at the bowling, while others play defensively.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to block is to play a dead-bat defensive stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of cast metal.

clue.text: Craving liquor for half a decade

parts.note: lust is strong desire
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a drink over a five-year stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin term for a five-year period, once marked by a Roman purification rite.

clue.text: Hang curtain at last to cut draught

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the drink, splitting it

parts.note: a swig is a big gulp or draught of drink

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of curtain

explanation.surface: Hang the drapes, then finish by blocking the cold air.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of 'curtain', goes into SWIG. 'draught' suggests a cold breeze, but it is a gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle and sway, or to be executed on the gallows.

clue.text: Subtle but false, the claims made by Jonson

indicators.note: false means the letters give a false picture until put right

explanation.surface: Ben Jonson's claims are clever yet untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: Subtle is the trickster title character of Ben Jonson's comedy The Alchemist, which 'made by Jonson' points to; 'subtle' looks like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle is the conman in Jonson's play who pretends to turn base metal into gold.

clue.text: Covered up? Strip off and admit passion

indicators.note: admit means let in, so one word takes the other inside

parts.note: to shed is to cast off a layer
heat is strong emotion or ardour

explanation.surface: Is it a cover-up? Get undressed and confess your desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admit' is the container signal. 'Strip off' sits against 'Covered up' as a contrast, tempting a solver to look for an undressing word as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Put into a protective case, as a sword goes into its scabbard.

clue.text: The emphatic hand of the Rev. Obadiah Slope?

definitions.text: The emphatic hand of the Rev. Obadiah Slope?

parts.words: The emphatic hand of the Rev. Obadiah Slope?
parts.note: the clergyman's surname suggests slanted handwriting, the slanting type used for stress

explanation.walkthrough: Obadiah Slope is the oily chaplain in Trollope's Barchester Towers; his surname points to sloping script.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanting typeface or handwriting, used in print to stress a word.
